sections.h2: What is the San Angelo city property tax rate?
sections.html:
The City of San Angelo's budget page lists its property tax rate at $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. That page sits beside the adopted budget for fiscal year 2026 to 2027 and a link to the Tom Green County Appraisal District's tool for breaking down your local bill.

The city share is one layer. The county, the school district and any other district on the parcel each add theirs, and the sum is what you owe. The same page also prints the local sales tax makeup, which comes to 8.25 percent including the state's 6.25 percent, and a hotel occupancy rate of 7 percent for the city.

City finance is at City Hall, 72 W. College Ave., and a Taxpayer Impact Statement and a posting of tax rate and budget information are linked from the budget page.

sections.h2: Where do I pay and appeal San Angelo property tax?
sections.html:
San Angelo is in Tom Green County, and two offices matter. The Tom Green Central Appraisal District is at 2302 Pulliam, and the county's Tax Assessor-Collector office is at 113 West Beauregard, with the main office open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. according to the county's page.

The appraisal district explains the online route: open your account, choose the Tax Summary tab, and use the pay link that appears when taxes are due. You can pay by electronic check or by card. The district also hosts a tax estimator and a protest process page.

  • The district lists May 15 as the protest deadline for many residential properties, and its notice told owners to email, mail, drop off or file on its website.
  • Your Notice of Appraised Value shows the deadline for your specific property.
  • The district also keeps drop boxes for payments and document drop-off.

sections.h2: What if the review board does not lower my San Angelo value?
sections.html: You still have three routes. The first is a suit in district court. The second is binding arbitration. The third is the State Office of Administrative Hearings, which takes cases where the review board value is over $1,000,000. In each case, pay at least the undisputed tax by the delinquency date, or the appeal can be put at risk. Keep every notice, because the appraisal district's records and your own photos of condition are the evidence that carries weight.

sections.h2: What dates and penalties apply in San Angelo?
sections.html:
Bills go out in October. Texas treats unpaid tax as delinquent on February 1, and the Comptroller says most owners must pay by January 31. On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added.

The penalty then grows by a point each month to 12 percent on July 1, while interest accrues at one percent a month with no limit. A private attorney under contract with a taxing unit can charge up to 20 percent more. For older or disabled homeowners, four installments are allowed, with the first due by February 1.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter most to San Angelo homeowners?
sections.html:
San Angelo skews older, with 16.8 percent of residents 65 or over and 7,069 veterans counted by the Census, so the age and veteran breaks do real work here. School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, plus an extra $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled, and cities or counties can add their own.

  • A homestead's appraised value cannot grow more than 10 percent a year once the exemption is in place.
  • A school tax freeze keeps the tax on a senior's home from rising above the amount set in the year they qualified.
  • A disabled veteran's exemption ranges from $5,000 for a rating of 10 to 29 percent up to $12,000 at 70 percent or more, and a 100 percent rating can earn a total homestead exemption.

The appraisal district publishes an explanation of the homestead cap on its site, and applications to the district are due by April 30. The Comptroller's exemptions page has the statewide list.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning in San Angelo?
sections.html:
The Census describes a moderate-cost ownership market in San Angelo. It counts 39,474 households averaging 2.41 people, and the median selected monthly cost is $1,536 for owners with a mortgage and $598 for those without. Median gross rent is $1,153.

  • 83.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is modest.
  • 61.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied.
  • The median household earns $65,864 a year.

Those figures describe the whole city, and a house on the north side of the river can sit well above or below them. A written offer or a local agent's pricing opinion tells you more than a citywide median.

sections.h2: What shaped San Angelo's housing stock?
sections.html:
The town began in the late 1860s across the North Concho River from Fort Concho, which opened in 1867. A trading post there grew into San Angelo, and the 1882 flood that wiped out the courthouse in nearby Ben Ficklin helped move the county seat to the new town. The railroad arrived in 1888, and the city incorporated in 1903.

Wool, cattle, and later oil built the economy, and the Permian Basin oil boom of 1923 helped double the population between 1920 and 1930 to 25,308. Another jump followed in 1940, when the War Department chose the city for Goodfellow Air Field. The state's historical handbook also credits the city with Angelo State University and a long-established medical sector.

Today the city has 100,640 people and has grown only 0.7 percent since 2020. Land area is 59.70 square miles, the mean commute is 19.2 minutes, and median household income is $65,864.

sections.h2: What happens to San Angelo property taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien attaches on January 1 and stays with the house, so the buyer cannot obtain clean title until what is owed is paid. Whoever owned the property on that date remains liable for the tax even after the sale.

The title company asks the tax office for a payoff and pays it at closing from the proceeds. A deed or related instrument is recorded with the county clerk, where the state manual lists a first-page recording fee of $5.00, and $4.00 for each extra page. Ask the appraisal district's tax office for a statement showing every unit's balance before you set a closing date.

Behind on San Angelo property tax and short on time? A written cash offer can account for the payoff so the sale does not stall.

faqs.q: What is San Angelo's city tax rate per $100?
faqs.a: The city's budget page shows $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. County, school district and other district rates are added on top, so your full bill is higher.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my San Angelo property tax online?
faqs.a: Use the Tom Green Central Appraisal District's account lookup, open the Tax Summary tab and select the pay link. It accepts electronic check and cards, and drop boxes are available at the office.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline in San Angelo?
faqs.a: The general Texas deadline is May 15 or 30 days after your notice was delivered, whichever is later. The appraisal district named May 15 as the cutoff for many residential properties, and your notice states your own date.

faqs.q: How much is the local sales tax in San Angelo?
faqs.a: The city's budget page puts the total at 8.25 percent. It breaks out as 1 percent for the city, 0.5 percent for the San Angelo Development Corporation, 0.5 percent for Tom Green County and 6.25 percent for the state.

faqs.q: Do back taxes stop me from selling my San Angelo house?
faqs.a: No. The tax lien means the amount owed is paid from the proceeds at closing. Request a payoff statement from the Tom Green Central Appraisal District's tax office so you know the number in advance.
